newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 22.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 43.34 points at 6,660.21 while the Nasdaq composite index fell more sharply.
* Strong first quarter earnings results are expected from the major oil companies because of refining profits.
* Advertising agency holding company Cordiant announced plans to split into two separate companies - Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising Worldwide and Bates Worldwide.
* ITT Industries said it agreed to buy Gould Pumps for $37 per share cash, or $815 million.

* Texaco said it expected to get a a refund of $700 million from the Internal Revenue Service because the U.S. Supreme Court let stand a lower court ruling that the oil company did not owe about $1 billion in taxes.
* Fidelty Investments said it named Robert Pozen, its general counsel, to replace J. Gary Burkhead as president and chief executive of the Fidelity Management and Research Co.
* Eli Lilly posted an 11 percent earnings gain to $432.6 million, or $0.79 per share, as new product sales helped offset a sales decline for its antidepressant Prozac.
* Ford plans to jointly develop a prototype hydrogen fuel cell vehicle with the U.S. Department of Energy that would get its power from a fuel cell instead of batteries.
* AST Research announced plans to cut more than 1,000 jobs because of worse-than-expected first quarter losses of $110 million.
* AT&T reported net income from continuing operations dropped 24 percent in the first quarter and that the second quarter would also come in short of earlier forecasts.
* Public sentiment has turned against the tobacco companies, giving politicians fresh impetus to oppose the industry, especially at the state and local level.
* The dollar fell as the mark firmed on concerns that the European monetary union might not go ahead as planned.
* Crude oil futures rose after Iraq said it would fly pilgrims home from the holy site of Mecca, Saudi Arabia.
* Tulane University and other private U.S. universities are structuring scholarships to draw top students.
